Only 22% of remote USD jobs list a pay figure. The rest are marked DOE—determined on experience. Here’s what that means for your salary negotiation.

According to Loker Dollar’s remote-job listings, 22% (940) of 4,280 active listings state a concrete USD salary. The remaining 78% (3,340) leave pay blank, signaling a DOE arrangement. This can be a chance to aim higher—if you know how to negotiate.

DOE gives employers flexibility, but it also lets you anchor on the high end of market rates. With rare skills like AI or data analysis, you can push above averages. One example: Online Consumer Panels America offers $25–$45/hour for product assessments—the only pay-disclosed listing in our sample of 7.

To negotiate effectively: research global benchmarks, quantify your impact, anchor with a range, ask about total compensation, and reference industry trends. DOE isn’t a red flag—it’s a lever.
